EXPLANATION: Two intense C–H stretches at 2888 / 2918 cm⁻¹ (rule GFQ-003) without a band near 2960 cm⁻¹ indicate molecules that contain CH₂ groups but essentially no CH₃ groups. Among the candidates only 1 (O-CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂-O, 1,4-butanediol) and 3–4 lack methyl groups, but 3 (morpholine) has no O–H, whereas the spectrum shows two strong C–O stretches at 1079 and 1015 cm⁻¹ typical of primary alcohols. Peak pairs at 1441/1479 cm⁻¹ match CH₂ scissoring/ wagging modes, and bands at 826 and 893 cm⁻¹ correspond to CH₂ rocking and C–C–O vibrations often seen in aliphatic diols. Taken together, the absence of CH₃ signals, presence of two primary-alcohol C–O stretches, and overall pattern of CH₂ vibrations best fit the simple, CH₂-only diol OCCCCO.
